title: `message` tests can be migrated from python to JS
body:
See https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/47498 for an example of such a migration
`pseudo-tty` tests can migrate as well, but that will require some more work using something like https://github.com/microsoft/node-pty or similar

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
@participant1 Once you’ve checked out the `node` repo and built, run

```shell
tools/test.py -J --mode=release message
```

To run all the `message` tests. At the moment, now that https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/47498 has landed there are only 26 left.

These aren’t tests written in Python; they’re tests that are _run_ by the Python script `tools/test.py`, but in a special way different from all the other tests in the Node codebase. The Python code runs all the `.js` files within `test/message` and compares their outputs against the matching `.out` files in the same folder, using a complicated regex pattern. Whenever the regex comparison fails, the test fails.

We don’t want to have all this logic in Python, so we’ve been migrating the `test/message` tests to use a new pattern where the regex comparison is done in JavaScript; the https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/47498 PR created a new helper to do that comparison, and migrated a few dozen tests to use it. The work that remains is to migrate the rest of the `message` tests, following the example of https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/47498.

> > @participant1 Sure! I would love to collaborate on it!
> > Any way we can keep in touch and coordinate?
> 
> Sure, I'll email you some options to connect.

@participant4 

I believe we can collaborate on the PR https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/47868 Most of the work has already been done.

Look for the conversation we are having there. In summary, @reporter needs to have as little diff as possible on the PR so what I have been trying to do is reverting the .snapshot files to contain the same exact content as their pair .out file, and also make the .js files contain the same code as their counterparts in the /message directory. Then I need to make sure the .mjs files created validate the tests migrated, meaning, all the tests migrated pass.

To run the tests just use the following command:

./node test/parallel/<TEST__BUNDLE_NAME>.mjs

What this will do is run the code in this file which implements the testing workflow developed by @reporter by running the .js files and validating their output with their corresponding .snapshot file. If the outputs are different, we need to modify the .mjs files to filter and clean the output of the .js file so it matches the .snapshot. I believed the .snapshots could be updated since the output of the .js was already validated, but the .snapshot must stay the same as the old .out files.

You don’t need to create another PR for this, unless of course you want to address the whole issue by yourself, which I would understand too.

Let me know if you have any other questions.
